It is an established practice to take old theorems about ordinary homology, and generalise them so as to obtain theorems about generalised homology theories.

J. F. Adams, [Ada3]

# Chromatic aberrations of geometric Satake over the regular locusThanks: Part of this work was done when the author was supported by the PD Soros Fellowship and NSF DGE-2140743. The present article is a preliminary version, so any comments and suggestions for improving it are greatly appreciated! I’ll post major updates to the arXiv, but I’ll upload minor edits to my website at https://sanathdevalapurkar.github.io/files/grG-regular.pdf; so please see there for the most up-to-date version.

**Authors:** S. K. Devalapurkar Address: 1 Oxford St, Cambridge, MA 02139 Email address: sdevalapurkar@math.harvard.edu, August 24, 2026

## Abstract

Let $G$ be a connected, simply-laced, almost simple algebraic group over $\mathbf{C}$ , let $G_{c}$ be a maximal compact subgroup of $G(\mathbf{C})$ , and let $T_{c}$ be a maximal torus therein. Let $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ denote the affine Grassmannian of $G$ , and let ${\check{{G}}}$ denote the Langlands dual group to $G$ with Lie algebra ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}$ . The derived geometric Satake equivalence of Bezrukavnikov-Finkelberg gives an equivalence between the $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Loc}_{G_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{C})$ of $G_{c}$ -equivariant local systems of $\mathbf{C}$ -vector spaces on $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ and the $\infty$ -category of quasicoherent sheaves on a large open substack of ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}[2]/{\check{{G}}}$ . In this article, we study the analogous story when $\mathrm{Loc}_{G_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{C})$ is replaced by the $\infty$ -category of $T_{c}$ -equivariant local systems of $k$ -modules over $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}(\mathbf{C})$ , where $k$ is ( $2$ -periodic) rational cohomology, (complex) K-theory, or elliptic cohomology. Crucial to our work is the genuine equivariant refinement of these cohomology theories. We show that, although there may not be an equivalence as in derived geometric Satake, the $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ admits a $1$ -parameter degeneration to an $\infty$ -category of quasicoherent sheaves built out of the geometry of various Langlands-dual stacks associated to $k$ and the $1$ -dimensional group scheme computing $S^{1}$ -equivariant $k$ -cohomology. For example, when $k$ is an elliptic cohomology theory with elliptic curve $E$ , the $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ degenerates to the $\infty$ -category of quasicoherent sheaves on a large open locus in the moduli stack of ${\check{{B}}}$ -bundles of degree $0$ on $E$ . We also study several applications of these equivalences, including: relating the generalized equivariant homology of $\mathrm{Gr}_{T}$ to generalizations of the Weyl algebra on a torus; proving multiplicative and elliptic versions of the Gelfand-Graev action on the affine closure of the cotangent bundle of the basic affine space; the interaction between power operations (like Steenrod and Adams operations) and derived geometric Satake; relations to work of Brylinski-Zhang and stable splittings of compact Lie groups; and the analogy to work of Hopkins-Kuhn-Ravenel.

## 1. Introduction

### 1.1. The derived geometric Satake equivalence

Let $G$ be a semisimple algebraic group over $\mathbf{C}$ , and let $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ denote the affine Grassmannian, defined as the quotient $G(\mathbf{C}(\!(t)\!))/G(\mathbf{C}[\![t]\!])=:G(\!(t)\!)/G[\![t]\!]$ . The geometric Satake equivalence of Mirkovic-Vilonen states:

#### Theorem 1.1 (Mirkovic-Vilonen, [MV]).

Let ${\check{{G}}}_{\mathbf{Z}}$ denote the smooth split reductive group scheme over $\mathbf{Z}$ whose root datum is dual to that of $G$ . Then there is an equivalence of symmetric monoidal abelian categories

$$ \mathrm{Perv}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{Z})\simeq\mathrm{Rep}({\check{{G}}}_{\mathbf{Z}}). $$

The abelian category $\mathrm{Perv}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{Z})$ arises as the heart of a $t$ -structure on the stable $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Shv}^{c}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{Z})$ of $G[\![t]\!]$ -equivariant constructible sheaves on $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ . However, Theorem 1.1 does not lift to an equivalence of stable $\infty$ -categories between $\mathrm{Shv}^{c}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{Z})$ and the derived $\infty$ -category of $\mathrm{Rep}({\check{{G}}}_{\mathbf{Z}})$ . Nevertheless, one has:

#### Theorem 1.2 (Bezrukavnikov-Finkelberg, [BF]).

Let ${\check{{G}}}={\check{{G}}}_{\mathbf{C}}$ . There is a $\mathbf{C}$ -linear equivalence of monoidal stable $\infty$ -categories

$$ \mathrm{Shv}^{c}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{C})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}[2]/{\check{{G}}}). $$

Here, ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}[2]$ denotes the derived scheme given by ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}$ placed in (homological) degree $2$ . Using Koszul duality, the right-hand side can be rewritten as

$$ \mathrm{Perf}({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}[2]/{\check{{G}}})\simeq\mathrm{Coh}((\{0\}\times_{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}\{0\})/{\check{{G}}}). $$

In [CR, Theorem 6.6.1], it was shown that the above equivalence can be refined to an equivalence of monoidal factorization stable $\infty$ -categories. (We will not need this refinement here, and only mention it for the sake of completeness.) There are several variants of Theorem 1.2 which have been proved in the literature; of relevance to us is a theorem from [ABG] concerning the Iwahori subgroup $I$ of $G[\![t]\!]$ . Namely, fix a Borel subgroup $B\subseteq G$ with unipotent radical $N$ , and let $I=G[\![t]\!]\times_{G}B$ . Then:

#### Theorem 1.3 (Arkhipov-Bezrukavnikov-Ginzburg, [ABG]).

There is an equivalence

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{I}^{c}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{C})\simeq\mathrm{Coh}((\widetilde{{\check{{\mathcal{N}}}}}\times_{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}\{0\})/{\check{{G}}}), $$

where $\widetilde{{\check{{\mathcal{N}}}}}=T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{B}}})$ is the Springer resolution. Using Koszul duality, the right-hand side can be rewritten as

$$ \mathrm{Coh}((\widetilde{{\check{{\mathcal{N}}}}}\times_{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}\{0\})/{\check{{G}}})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}_{\mathbf{C}}[2]/{\check{{G}}}_{\mathbf{C}}), $$

where $\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}_{\mathbf{C}}[2]={\check{{G}}}\times^{{\check{{B}}}}{\check{{\mathfrak{n}}}}^{\perp}[2]$ is a shifted analogue of the Grothendieck-Springer resolution.

The equivalences of Theorem 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 admit simpler analogues, where one considers the full subcategories of the ind-completions of $\mathrm{Shv}^{c}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{C})$ and $\mathrm{Shv}^{c}_{I}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{C})$ generated by the constant sheaf. Let us denote these $\infty$ -categories by $\mathrm{Loc}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{C})$ and $\mathrm{Loc}_{I}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{C})$ ; they are categories of $G[\![t]\!]$ - and $I$ -equivariant local systems of complexes of $\mathbf{C}$ -vector spaces on $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ . The notion of “local system” here must be interpreted in the derived sense, as (equivariant) representations of the fundamental $\infty$ -groupoid of $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ , and not of its fundamental groupoid (which would be trivial if $G$ is simply-connected). As we will discuss in the body of the article, the above results then restrict to equivalences

$$ \displaystyle\mathrm{Loc}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{C}) \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast,\mathrm{reg}}[2]/{\check{{G}}}), \displaystyle\mathrm{Loc}_{I}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{C}) \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh(\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}^{\mathrm{reg}}[2]/{\check{{G}}}). $$

Here, ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast,\mathrm{reg}}$ denotes the open subscheme of regular elements in ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}$ , i.e., those elements whose stabilizer under the coadjoint action of ${\check{{G}}}$ has dimension given by the rank of ${\check{{G}}}$ ; and similarly for $\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}^{\mathrm{reg}}$ . We will refer to these equivalences as the derived geometric Satake equivalence (resp. the ABG equivalence) over the regular locus. In fact, one can can give a proof of Theorem 1.2 using 1.1 combined with the fact that ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast,\mathrm{reg}}$ has complement of large codimension in ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}$ (see [Dev3, Section 3.2]).

Our goal in this article is to study an analogue of the derived geometric Satake equivalence over the regular locus where $\mathbf{C}$ is replaced by other ring (spectra) of coefficients. The observation allowing us to do this is that the $\infty$ -categories $\mathrm{Loc}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{C})$ and $\mathrm{Loc}_{I}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{C})$ are homotopy-theoretic in nature. Indeed, they depend only on the $G[\![t]\!]$ -equivariant (resp. $I$ -equivariant) homotopy type of $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ . This, in turn can be understood using a result of Quillen and Garland-Raghunathan (see [GR2, Mit]), which gives a homotopy equivalence $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}\simeq\Omega G_{c}$ (and a homeomorphism onto the subspace of $\Omega G_{c}$ on those based loops with polynomial Fourier expansion); so all computations reduce to homotopy-theoretic statements about $\Omega G_{c}$ . Here, $G_{c}\subseteq G(\mathbf{C})$ is a maximal compact subgroup. Since $G[\![t]\!]$ is homotopy equivalent to $G_{c}$ (and $I$ is homotopy equivalent to a maximal torus $T_{c}\subseteq G_{c}$ ), the equivalences 1.1 and 1.2 can be restated as a pair of equivalences

$$ \displaystyle\mathrm{Loc}_{G_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{C}) \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast,\mathrm{reg}}[2]/{\check{{G}}}), \displaystyle\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{C}) \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh(\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}^{\mathrm{reg}}[2]/{\check{{G}}}). $$

### 1.2. A K-theoretic and elliptic variant

As mentioned above, our goal in this article is to generalize the equivalence 1.2 to the case of K-theoretic and elliptic cohomology coefficients. In order to motivate the discussion, we need to review some of the setup of equivariant generalized cohomology. (For the homotopy theorists: it is exactly the genuine nature of equivariant generalized cohomology which lends substance to results like Theorem 1.4 below.)

If $G_{c}$ is a compact Lie group, Atiyah and Segal defined $G_{c}$ -equivariant complex K-theory $\mathrm{KU}_{G_{c}}$ in [Seg, AS]: this is a generalized cohomology theory, viewed as a spectrum in the sense of homotopy theory, which classifies $G_{c}$ -equivariant vector bundles on finite $G_{c}$ -spaces. Direct sum and tensor products of $G$ -equivariant vector bundles equips $\mathrm{KU}_{G_{c}}$ with the structure of a ring spectrum; in fact, it is an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring, meaning (for instance) that the multiplication on cohomology can be refined by Adams operations. Despite its definition, the geometric interpretation of cocycles for equivariant K-theory as equivariant vector bundles will play no role below.

Two important examples are the following. When $G_{c}$ is the trivial group, $\mathrm{KU}_{G_{c}}$ is simply periodic complex K-theory $\mathrm{KU}$ , and Bott periodicity gives a graded isomorphism $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{KU}\cong\mathbf{Z}[\beta^{\pm 1}]$ with the Bott class $\beta$ in weight $2$ . On the other hand, when $G_{c}$ is a connected compact Lie group with complex representation ring $\mathrm{RU}(G_{c})$ , the coefficient ring $\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{KU}_{G_{c}}$ is the tensor product $\mathrm{RU}(G_{c})\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}}\mathbf{Z}[\beta^{\pm 1}]$ . In particular, if $G_{c}$ is a compact torus $T_{c}$ , then $\spec\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{KU}_{T_{c}}$ is the corresponding algebraic torus $T_{\mathbf{Z}[\beta^{\pm 1}]}$ over $\mathbf{Z}[\beta^{\pm 1}]$ .

In Section 3, we define a $\mathrm{KU}$ -linear $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KU})$ of $T_{c}$ -equivariant local systems of $\mathrm{KU}$ -modules on $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ ; this should be viewed as a $\mathrm{KU}$ -theoretic analogue of the $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Loc}_{I}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KU})$ . The ideal analogue of 1.2 would identify $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KU})$ with the $\infty$ -category of perfect complexes on some stack over $\mathrm{KU}$ defined in terms of the Langlands dual group. Unfortunately, we do not know how to define this putative stack over $\mathrm{KU}$ ; instead, we will study a particular degeneration of this $\infty$ -category, denoted $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KU})$ . The reason for studying this degeneration is explained in the introduction to Section 4; we will also discuss its “philosophical” meaning momentarily. For the moment, let us just note the utility of this degeneration: while $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KU})$ is a $\mathrm{KU}$ -linear $\infty$ -category, $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KU})$ is instead an ordinary ( $\mathbf{Z}$ -linear) $\infty$ -category; so we do not have to be concerned with questions such as the definition of the dual group over $\mathrm{KU}$ .

Exactly the same setup works if $k$ is a complex oriented $2$ -periodic ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring which is an elliptic cohomology theory (in the sense of [Lur1, GM1, GM2]) with associated elliptic curve $E$ over $\pi_{0}(k)$ . Namely, we construct a $k$ -linear $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ , as well as a degeneration $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ which is instead an ordinary ( $\pi_{0}(k)$ -linear) $\infty$ -category. In both this case and the case of $\mathrm{KU}$ , an object $\mathcal{F}\in\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ defines a corresponding object $\mathcal{F}^{\mathrm{gr}}\in\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ , and there is a spectral sequence

$$ \pi_{\ast}(k)\otimes_{\pi_{0}(k)}\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{Map}_{\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)}(\underline{k}^{\mathrm{gr}},\mathcal{F}^{\mathrm{gr}})\Rightarrow\pi_{\ast}\mathrm{Map}_{\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)}(\underline{k},\mathcal{F})=\pi_{\ast}\Gamma_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathcal{F}). $$

Here, $\underline{k}$ denotes the constant sheaf.

To state our main result, we need a small observation. Suppose $G$ is a connected, almost simple, and simply-laced algebraic group over $\mathbf{C}$ , and let ${\check{{G}}}_{\mathbf{C}}$ denote the Langlands dual over $\mathbf{C}$ . Then ${\check{{G}}}_{\mathbf{C}}$ is centrally isogeneous to $G$ . For instance, if $G$ is simply-connected, ${\check{{G}}}_{\mathbf{C}}$ is the quotient of $G$ by its center. In general (under the simply-laced hypothesis), the action of $G$ on itself by conjugation descends/ascends to an action of ${\check{{G}}}_{\mathbf{C}}$ . In particular, the action of $T_{\mathbf{C}}$ on $G$ by conjugation descends/ascends to an action of ${\check{{T}}}_{\mathbf{C}}$ on $G$ . Therefore, if $T_{c}$ denote the maximal compact subgroup of $T_{\mathbf{C}}$ (and similarly for ${\check{{T}}}_{c}$ ), then the conjugation action of $T_{c}$ on $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ descends/ascends to an action of ${\check{{T}}}_{c}$ on $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ .

The main result of this article is the following.

#### Theorem 1.4 (Corollary 6.8, Corollary 7.10, Corollary 8.11).

Suppose $G$ is a connected, almost simple, and simply-laced algebraic group over $\mathbf{C}$ . Let $T\subseteq G$ be a maximal torus, and let ${\check{{T}}}_{c}$ denote a maximal compact subgroup of the Langlands dual torus over $\mathbf{C}$ . Let $k$ denote either $2$ -periodified rational cohomology $\mathbf{Q}[u^{\pm 1}]$ , complex K-theory $\mathrm{KU}$ , or elliptic cohomology with associated elliptic curve $E$ , and let $F$ be an algebraically closed field over $\pi_{0}(k)$ . Then there are equivalences

$$ \displaystyle\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{T}}}_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{Q}[u^{\pm 1}])\otimes_{\mathbf{Q}}F \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh(\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}^{{}^{\prime},\mathrm{reg}}/{\check{{G}}}), \displaystyle\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{T}}}_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KU})\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}}F \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh(\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{reg}}/{\check{{G}}}), \displaystyle\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{T}}}_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)\otimes_{\pi_{0}(k)}F \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh(\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{B}}}}^{0}(E)^{\mathrm{reg}}). $$

Here, the dual groups on the right-hand side are defined over $F$ ; the final equivalence is assuming that $k$ is an elliptic cohomology theory; $\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}^{{}^{\prime}}$ denotes ${\check{{G}}}\times^{{\check{{B}}}}{\check{{\mathfrak{b}}}}$ ; $\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}$ denotes ${\check{{G}}}\times^{{\check{{B}}}}{\check{{B}}}$ for the conjugation action of ${\check{{B}}}$ on itself11 1 We warn the reader that the symbol $\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}$ will mean ${\check{{G}}}\times^{{\check{{B}}}}{\check{{B}}}$ only in the introduction; it has a slightly different meaning in the body of the article, described in Definition 7.1.; $\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{B}}}}^{0}(E)$ denotes the moduli stack of degree zero ${\check{{B}}}$ -bundles on $E$ ; and the adornment $\mathrm{reg}$ denotes an open “regular” locus whose complement has codimension $2$ .

Since $T_{c}$ and ${\check{{T}}}_{c}$ are isogeneous by a finite group, there is no difference between $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{Q}[u^{\pm 1}])$ and $\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{T}}}_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{Q}[u^{\pm 1}])$ . Therefore, the first part of Theorem 1.4 is, of course, just 1.4 (once one identifies $\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}^{{}^{\prime}}\cong\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}$ ). However, we warn the reader that if $k$ is not $\mathbf{Q}[u^{\pm 1}]$ , the categories $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ and $\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{T}}}_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ are generally genuinely different, and do not agree even upon base-change along $\pi_{0}(k)\to F$ .

#### Remark 1.5.

The same argument used to prove Theorem 1.4 shows that if $G$ is a connected, almost simple, and simply-laced algebraic group over $\mathbf{C}$ with torsion-free fundamental group, and $k$ denotes either $2$ -periodified rational cohomology $\mathbf{Q}[u^{\pm 1}]$ , complex K-theory $\mathrm{KU}$ , or elliptic cohomology with associated elliptic curve $E$ , then there are equivalences

$$ \displaystyle\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{G}}}_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{Q}[u^{\pm 1}])\otimes_{\mathbf{Q}}F \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\mathrm{reg}}/{\check{{G}}}), \displaystyle\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{G}}}_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KU})\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}}F \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh({\check{{G}}}^{\mathrm{reg}}/{\check{{G}}}), \displaystyle\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{G}}}_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)\otimes_{\pi_{0}(k)}F \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh(\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(E)^{\mathrm{reg}}), $$

where $\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(E)^{\mathrm{reg}}\subseteq\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(E)$ is a particular open substack of the moduli stack of semistable degree zero ${\check{{G}}}$ -bundles on $E$ . More generally, our arguments are easily modified to show that if $L$ is the Levi quotient of a parabolic subgroup $P\subseteq G$ and $L$ has torsion-free fundamental group, then there are equivalences

$$ \displaystyle\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{L}}}_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{Q}[u^{\pm 1}])\otimes_{\mathbf{Q}}F \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh(\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}_{{\check{{P}}}}^{{}^{\prime},\mathrm{reg}}/{\check{{P}}}), \displaystyle\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{L}}}_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KU})\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}}F \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh(\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}_{{\check{{P}}}}^{\mathrm{reg}}/{\check{{P}}}), \displaystyle\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{L}}}_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)\otimes_{\pi_{0}(k)}F \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh(\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{P}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(E)^{\mathrm{reg}}), $$

where $\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}_{{\check{{P}}}}^{{}^{\prime}}$ denotes ${\check{{G}}}\times^{{\check{{P}}}}{\check{{\mathfrak{p}}}}$ ; $\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}_{{\check{{P}}}}$ denotes ${\check{{G}}}\times^{{\check{{P}}}}{\check{{P}}}$ for the conjugation action of ${\check{{P}}}$ on itself; and $\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{P}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(E)$ denotes the moduli stack of degree zero semistable ${\check{{P}}}$ -bundles on $E$ . The equivalence concerning $\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{L}}}_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{Q}[u^{\pm 1}])$ above is closely related to the parabolic variant of Theorem 1.3 which can be deduced from [CD].

Theorem 1.4 also gives an analogue of [BF, Theorem 4]. Namely, the stacks ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}/{\check{{G}}}$ , ${\check{{G}}}/{\check{{G}}}$ , and $\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(E)$ each have a canonical map to $B{\check{{G}}}$ ; let $\QCoh_{\mathrm{free}}({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}/{\check{{G}}})$ , $\QCoh_{\mathrm{free}}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{G}}})$ , and $\QCoh_{\mathrm{free}}(\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(E))$ denote the essential images of the resulting pullback functors from $\mathrm{Rep}({\check{{G}}})$ to $\QCoh({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}/{\check{{G}}})$ , $\QCoh({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{G}}})$ , and $\QCoh(\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(E))$ . Then, we show:

#### Corollary 1.6 (Corollary 6.19, Corollary 7.20, and Corollary 8.20).

In the setting of Theorem 1.4, let $F$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero over $\pi_{0}(k)$ . Then there is a $t$ -structure on $\mathrm{Loc}_{G_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ such that there are fully faithful embeddings

$$ \displaystyle\QCoh_{\mathrm{free}}({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}/{\check{{G}}})^{\heartsuit} \displaystyle\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{G}}}_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{Q}[u^{\pm 1}])^{\heartsuit}\otimes_{\mathbf{Q}}F, \displaystyle\QCoh_{\mathrm{free}}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{G}}})^{\heartsuit} \displaystyle\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{G}}}_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KU})^{\heartsuit}\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}}F, \displaystyle\QCoh_{\mathrm{free}}(\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(E))^{\heartsuit} \displaystyle\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{G}}}_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)^{\heartsuit}\otimes_{\pi_{0}(k)}F. $$

When ${\check{{G}}}$ is not of type $E_{8}$ , we explicitly identify the essential image of these embeddings in terms of a topologically defined subcategory of $\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{G}}}_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)^{\heartsuit}\otimes_{\pi_{0}(k)}F$ .

In the case of K-theory, this is similar to the expectations of [CK]. Again, just as in Remark 1.5, there are also parabolic versions of these embeddings. In the case of $2$ -periodic rational cohomology, one obtains an upgrade (as in [BF, Theorem 2]): namely, if $\mathrm{HC}^{\hbar,\mathrm{free}}_{{\check{{G}}}}$ denotes the category of Harish-Chandra bimodules of the form $U_{\hbar}({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}})\otimes V$ for $V\in\mathrm{Rep}({\check{{G}}})$ , then there is a fully faithful embedding

$$ (\mathrm{HC}^{\hbar,\mathrm{free}}_{{\check{{G}}}})^{\heartsuit}\hookrightarrow\mathrm{Loc}_{G_{c}\times S^{1}_{\mathrm{rot}}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)^{\heartsuit}. $$

See Corollary 6.32 and the discussion surrounding it. At least in the case $G=\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ , one can similarly relate a category of Harish-Chandra bimodules for the quantum group to $\mathrm{Loc}_{G_{c}\times S^{1}_{\mathrm{rot}}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KU})^{\heartsuit}$ (see Proposition 7.33).

#### Remark 1.7.

We also study the effect of power operations (like Steenrod and Adams operations) on $k$ under the Langlands duality of Theorem 1.4. The reader is referred to Theorem 9.11 for a precise statement, but let us just mention here that using the theory of degree $p$ isogenies on $\mathbf{G}_{a}$ , $\mathbf{G}_{m}$ , and the elliptic curve $E$ , we show that power operations on $k$ correspond under Theorem 1.4 to natural “Artin-Schreier” maps on $\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}^{\prime}/{\check{{G}}}$ , $\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}/{\check{{G}}}$ , and $\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{B}}}}^{0}(E)$ . (This is different, but related to, Lonergan’s work in [Lon4]: we only consider power operations on $k$ , while Lonergan considers power operations on the entire ${\mathbf{E}_{{3}}}$ -algebra $k^{G_{c}}[\mathrm{Gr}_{G}]$ ; we will address the latter situation in future work.)

#### Remark 1.8.

Let us mention some previous work towards analogues of the geometric Satake equivalence with other coefficients. For instance, an early paper in the context of geometric representation theory is [GKV1]. A conjecture about complex K-theoretic geometric Satake was proposed in [CK]; in a similar vein, a discussion of the K-theoretic case is the content of the talk [Lon3]. In [YZ1], Yang and Zhao study a higher chromatic analogue of quantum groups, and it would be interesting to study the relationship between the present article and their work. After the first version of this paper was written, the preprint [Zho] was posted on the arXiv; it is concerned with ideas similar to the ones studied here.

The proofs of the equivalences in Theorem 1.4 with $\mathbf{Q}[u^{\pm 1}]$ -coefficients follow from the work of Bezrukavnikov-Finkelberg-Mirkovic [BFM] and Yun-Zhu [YZ2]; and the proofs of the equivalences involving $\mathrm{KU}$ follow from the aforementioned work of Bezrukavnikov-Finkelberg-Mirkovic. However, the approaches taken in these references rely either on the geometric Satake equivalence (for which there is no existing analogue with coefficients in $\mathrm{KU}$ or elliptic cohomology), or on a geometric interpretation of cycles in the relevant cohomology theory (for which there is no known analogue in elliptic cohomology). We therefore reprove these results in the present article so as to provide a uniform approach to all the equivalences of Theorem 1.4 and of Remark 1.5.

#### Remark 1.9.

In Section 10, we also study a degeneration $\mathrm{Loc}_{G_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(G_{c};k)$ of the category $\mathrm{Loc}_{G_{c}}(G_{c};k)$ of conjugation-equivariant locally constant sheaves on $G_{c}$ . Namely, we show that (at least if $G_{c}$ has torsion-free fundamental group) $\mathrm{Loc}_{G_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(G_{c};k)$ is equivalent to the category of quasicoherent sheaves on the additive (resp. multiplicative; resp. elliptic) regular centralizer group scheme for ${\check{{G}}}$ if $k=\mathbf{Q}[u^{\pm 1}]$ (resp. $k=\mathrm{KU}$ ; resp. $k$ is an elliptic cohomology theory). Motivated by [NZ] and [GPS, Theorem 1.1], one can heuristically interpret our discussion as describing a version of mirror symmetry for the wrapped Fukaya category of the symplectic stack $T^{\ast}(G_{c}/G_{c})$ , albeit with coefficients in the complex-oriented $2$ -periodic ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring $k$ . Namely, the “ $k$ -theoretic” mirror to $T^{\ast}(G_{c}/G_{c})$ is the appropriate variant of the regular centralizer group scheme for the Langlands dual group.

Let us now discuss further the degeneration of the $\mathrm{KU}$ -linear $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ to $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ . This can be explained in ‘‘two’’ ways22 2 The quotes are to indicate that these two approaches are really the same; since it would be too digressive to do so here, we will explain the meaning of this (admittedly cryptic) statement in a sequel to this article.:

- (a) One important lesson from chromatic homotopy theory is that the stable homotopy groups of spheres are closely connected to the coherent cohomology of the moduli stack $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{fg}}$ of $1$ -dimensional formal groups. For instance, the Adams-Novikov spectral sequence can be restated as a spectral sequence

$$ E_{2}^{\ast,\ast}\cong\mathrm{H}^{\ast}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{fg}};\omega^{\otimes\ast})\Rightarrow\pi_{\ast}(S^{0}), $$

where $S^{0}$ is the sphere spectrum and $\omega$ is the line bundle of invariant differentials on the universal $1$ -dimensional formal group over $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{fg}}$ . This picture can in fact be categorified: the $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Sp}$ of spectra behaves like the $\infty$ -category $\QCoh(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{fg}})$ in a very precise sense33 3 This is not quite correct: namely, one has to instead replace $\QCoh(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{fg}})$ by the ind-completion of the thick subcategory of $\QCoh(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{fg}})$ generated by tensor powers of $\omega$ . For brevity, we will simply denote this variant category by $\QCoh(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{fg}})$ . In the homotopy theory literature, e.g., [Gre] or [BHS, Definition 5.14], this variant subcategory is often instead denoted by $\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{fg}})$ . However, the use of the symbol $\mathrm{IndCoh}(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{fg}})$ does not agree with the more established notion of ind-coherent sheaves from [GR1].. Namely, the Adams-Novikov spectral sequence is categorified by a $1$ -parameter degeneration of $\mathrm{Sp}$ into $\QCoh(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{fg}})$ ; see [Pst2, GWX, Gre]. Moreover, this degeneration can be constructed using the stable motivic category over $\mathbf{C}$ . This gives a precise sense in which “topology is approximated by algebra”. The degeneration of $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ into $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ is of exactly the same type. In fact, both degenerations ( $\mathrm{Sp}\leadsto\QCoh(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{fg}})$ and $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)\leadsto\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ ) can be constructed simultaneously using the even filtration of [HRW, Pst1], and we will address this point in a future article. (That is to say, the Adams-Novikov spectral sequence and 1.5 should both be regarded as special cases of a more general construction.)

- (b) In geometric representation theory, one often considers “graded lifts” of categories of ( $\mathbf{C}$ -valued, say) sheaves on a scheme/stack $X$ : this is generally defined as the category $\mathrm{Shv}^{\mathrm{mixed}}(X;\mathbf{C})$ of mixed sheaves on $X$ . See [BBD] and the more recent [HL]. It is generally expected, for instance, that there is a mixed variant of Theorem 1.2, stating that there is an equivalence $\mathrm{Shv}^{\mathrm{mixed}}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{C})\simeq\mathrm{Perf}({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}(2)/{\check{{G}}})$ , where ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}(2)/{\check{{G}}}$ is now a classical (not derived!) stack, except with a grading which places ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}(2)$ in weight $2$ . This grading can be ignored if we replace $\mathbf{C}$ by its $2$ -periodification. One can view $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ as a category of “mixed” $k$ -valued local systems. (So where is the grading? It is not visible on the right-hand sides of the equivalences in Theorem 1.4 is that the ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring $k$ is assumed to be $2$ -periodic; but the grading will reappear if we assume $k$ is ordinary (non-periodic) cohomology or connective K-theory as in [Dev3].) A natural question, of course, is to define a full $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Shv}_{I}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ which specializes to the usual category of mixed sheaves when $k=\mathbf{C}[u^{\pm 1}]$ ; we hope to address this in the future article referred to in the preceding bullet point.

The perspective of the degeneration $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)\leadsto\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ as being analogous to the degeneration $\mathrm{Sp}\leadsto\QCoh(\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{fg}})$ – and furthermore that both are related to the even filtration of [HRW, Pst1] – is very helpful, because it gives us an indication of how to define $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ when $k$ is not necessarily complex-oriented and $2$ -periodic. In particular, we also study the example of $k$ being real K-theory $\mathrm{KO}$ . This is an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring with somewhat complicated homotopy groups. Despite this, the ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring $\mathrm{KO}$ is itself easy to describe using $\mathrm{KU}$ : namely, there is an action of $\mathbf{Z}/2$ on $\mathrm{KU}$ by complex conjugation, and $\mathrm{KO}=\mathrm{KU}^{h\mathbf{Z}/2}$ . Moreover, just like the standard Adams-Novikov spectral sequence for the homotopy of the sphere spectrum, there is a spectral sequence

$$ E_{2}^{\ast,\ast}\cong\mathrm{H}^{\ast}(B\mathbf{Z}/2;\omega^{\ast})\Rightarrow\pi_{\ast}(\mathrm{KO}), $$

where $\omega$ is the line bundle over $B\mathbf{Z}/2$ given by the sign action of $\mathbf{Z}/2$ on $\mathbf{Z}$ ; in fact, this can be identified with the Adams-Novikov spectral sequence for the homotopy of $\mathrm{KO}$ . That is, the sphere spectrum is to $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{fg}}$ as $\mathrm{KO}$ is to $B\mathbf{Z}/2$ . There is also a good notion of $G_{c}$ -equivariant real K-theory.

Instead of constructing a degeneration of the $\mathrm{KO}$ -linear $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KO})$ into a graded $\pi_{\ast}(\mathrm{KO})$ -linear $\infty$ -category, one can construct a degeneration of $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KO})$ into a $\QCoh(B\mathbf{Z}/2)$ -module $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KO})$ . The construction of $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KO})$ is straightforward: the $\mathbf{Z}/2$ -action via complex conjugation on $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KU})$ defines a $\mathbf{Z}/2$ -action on $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KU})$ , and this defines the $\QCoh(B\mathbf{Z}/2)$ -module category $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KO})$ .

#### Proposition 1.10 (Proposition 7.25).

Let $\theta$ denote the involution on $\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}/{\check{{G}}}$ given on $\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}={\check{{G}}}\times^{{\check{{B}}}}{\check{{B}}}$ by $(g,x)\mapsto(g,x^{-1})$ , so that the quotient $(\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}/{\check{{G}}})/\langle{\theta}\rangle$ defines a stack over $B\mathbf{Z}/2$ . Then there is a $\QCoh(B\mathbf{Z}/2)$ -linear equivalence

$$ \mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{T}}}_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KO})\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}}F\simeq\QCoh((\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{reg}}/{\check{{G}}})/\langle{\theta}\rangle). $$

For instance, if $G=\mathrm{PGL}_{2}$ , so that $\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}$ is the moduli of pairs $(g,\ell)$ with $g\in\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ and $\ell=[x:y]\in\mathbf{P}^{1}$ is a line preserved by $g$ , the involution $\theta$ simply inverts $g$ . We also briefly discuss the case of coefficients in connective real K-theory $\mathrm{ko}$ .

Similarly, if one fixes a prime $p$ and sets $T_{c}[p^{\infty}]$ to be the $p$ -power torsion subgroup of $T_{c}$ , one can also define a $\QCoh(B\mathbf{Z}_{p}^{\times})$ -module category $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}[p^{\infty}]}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};L_{K(1)}S^{0})$ . This $\infty$ -category is a degeneration of the $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}[p^{\infty}]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};L_{K(1)}S^{0})$ of $T_{c}[p^{\infty}]$ -equivariant local systems of $L_{K(1)}S^{0}$ -modules on $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ , where $L_{K(1)}S^{0}=(\mathrm{KU}^{\wedge}_{p})^{h\mathbf{Z}_{p}^{\times}}$ is the $K(1)$ -local sphere (also known as the “image of J” spectrum) [Ada2, Rav]. In this case, let $\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}_{p^{\infty}}\subseteq\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}$ denote the locus of pairs $(g,{\check{{B}}}^{\prime})\in\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}$ where ${\check{{B}}}^{\prime}\subseteq{\check{{G}}}$ is a Borel subgroup containing $g$ such that the eigenvalues of $g$ are all $p$ -power roots of unity. Then there is a $\mathbf{Z}_{p}^{\times}\times{\check{{G}}}$ -action on $\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}_{p^{\infty}}$ , where $n\in\mathbf{Z}_{p}^{\times}$ acts by $(g,{\check{{B}}}^{\prime})\mapsto(g^{n},{\check{{B}}}^{\prime})$ , and Proposition 7.29 similarly states that a $\QCoh(B\mathbf{Z}_{p}^{\times})$ -linear equivalence

$$ \mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{T}}}_{c}[p^{\infty}]}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};L_{K(1)}S^{0})\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}_{p}}F\simeq\QCoh((\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}_{p^{\infty}}^{\mathrm{reg}}/{\check{{G}}})/\mathbf{Z}_{p}^{\times}). $$

The stack on the right-hand side can be thought of as an open substack in the moduli stack of ${\check{{B}}}$ -bundles on the $p$ -adic solenoid, modulo the natural symmetries (by $\mathbf{Z}_{p}^{\times}$ ) of this solenoid. In Remark 8.15, we make some speculations about the analogous picture when $L_{K(1)}S^{0}$ is replaced by the $K(n)$ -local sphere $L_{K(n)}S^{0}$ : the primary modification is that one must now consider the moduli stack of ${\check{{B}}}$ -bundles on the $p$ -adic $n$ -dimensional solenoid, modulo an action of the units in the division algebra over $\mathbf{Q}_{p}$ with Hasse invariant $1/n$ .

### 1.3. A unifying picture?

In this informal section, we suggest a picture which attempts to unify the various calculations in this article. Throughout, we will again take $G$ to be a connected, almost simple, and simply-laced algebraic group over $\mathbf{C}$ with torsion-free fundamental group, and $k$ will denote either $2$ -periodified rational cohomology $\mathbf{Q}[u^{\pm 1}]$ , complex K-theory $\mathrm{KU}$ , or elliptic cohomology with associated elliptic curve $E$ . (As long as the discussion below is interpreted correctly, one could even take $k$ to be (connective) real K-theory or the ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring of topological modular forms [DFHH].)

First, just as there is a degeneration of the $k$ -linear $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ to an ordinary ( $\pi_{0}(k)$ -linear) $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ , we expect to show in future work that there is a well-behaved $k$ -linear $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Shv}_{I}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ of Iwahori-equivariant sheaves on $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ , along with a degeneration to an ordinary $\pi_{0}(k)$ -linear $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Shv}_{I}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ . (This is related to the “faux” definition from [Dev3, Construction 3.7.15].) Just as in Theorem 1.4, we also hope to show that there are equivalences

$$ \displaystyle\mathrm{Shv}_{{\check{{I}}}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{Q}[u^{\pm 1}])\otimes_{\mathbf{Q}}F \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh(\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}^{{}^{\prime}}/{\check{{G}}}), \displaystyle\mathrm{Shv}_{{\check{{I}}}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KU})\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}}F \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh(\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}/{\check{{G}}}), \displaystyle\mathrm{Shv}_{{\check{{I}}}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)\otimes_{\pi_{0}(k)}F \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh(\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{B}}}}^{0}(E)); $$

there should also be similar equivalences when the Iwahori subgroup is replaced by standard parahorics in $L^{+}{\check{{G}}}$ . In particular, when ${\check{{I}}}$ is replaced by $L^{+}{\check{{G}}}$ , we expect to prove equivalences

$$ \displaystyle\mathrm{Shv}_{L^{+}{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathbf{Q}[u^{\pm 1}])\otimes_{\mathbf{Q}}F \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}/{\check{{G}}}), \displaystyle\mathrm{Shv}_{L^{+}{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};\mathrm{KU})\otimes_{\mathbf{Z}}F \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{G}}}), \displaystyle\mathrm{Shv}_{L^{+}{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)\otimes_{\pi_{0}(k)}F \displaystyle\simeq\QCoh(\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(E)). $$

Let us write $\mathrm{Bun}_{G}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})$ to denote either of the stacks $\mathfrak{g}/G$ , $G/G$ , and $\mathrm{Bun}_{G}^{\mathrm{ss}}(E)$ , depending on the choice of $k$ . See Remark 8.14 for an explanation of this notation: roughly, $\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee}$ is the stack of multiplicative line bundles on $\mathbf{G}_{0}=\mathbf{G}_{a}$ , $\mathbf{G}_{m}$ , or $E$ , respectively. Note that there is a map $\mathrm{Bun}_{G}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})\to BG$ ; in fact, it naturally lifts/descends to a stack $\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})^{\prime}$ defined over $B{\check{{G}}}$ . (For instance, if $k$ is $2$ -periodic rational cohomology or $\mathrm{KU}$ , then $\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})^{\prime}$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{g}/{\check{{G}}}\cong{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/{\check{{G}}}$ or $G/{\check{{G}}}$ , respectively.)

Suppose $P\subseteq G$ is a parabolic subgroup with Levi quotient $L$ (with torsion-free fundamental group), and let $I_{P}$ denote its preimage under the map $G[\![t]\!]\to G$ . Set $I_{P}^{0}$ to be the kernel of the composite $I_{P}\to P\to L$ , and ${\check{{P}}}\subseteq{\check{{G}}}$ to be the dual parabolic subgroup to $P$ . One can then similarly define a stack $\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{P}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})^{\prime}$ , and we expect to prove equivalences

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{I_{P}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)\otimes_{\pi_{0}(k)}F\simeq\QCoh(\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{P}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})^{\prime}). $$

If we replace $I_{P}$ on the left-hand side by $I_{P}^{0}$ , then $\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{P}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})^{\prime}$ must be replaced by the stack $\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{P}}}}^{\mathrm{ss},\mathrm{nil}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})^{\prime}$ defined as the fiber of the map $\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{P}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})^{\prime}\to\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{P}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})^{{}^{\prime},\mathrm{coarse}}$ over the basepoint of the trivial bundle. For instance, if $k$ is $2$ -periodic rational cohomology or $\mathrm{KU}$ , then $\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{P}}}}^{\mathrm{ss},\mathrm{nil}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})^{\prime}$ is isomorphic to $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}_{P}/{\check{{G}}}$ or $\widetilde{\mathcal{U}}_{P}/{\check{{G}}}$ , respectively, where $\widetilde{\mathcal{N}}_{P}$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal{U}}_{P}$ are the partial resolutions (à la [BM]) of the nilpotent and unipotent cones in $G$ , respectively.

The above discussion suggest the following informal picture, which I hope to make precise in future work. There should be a well-defined $(\infty,2)$ -category of “ $\infty$ -categories with an action of $\mathrm{Shv}(G(\!(t)\!);k)$ ” (this seems to be rather subtle to make sense of in the genuine equivariant setting), and it should admit a graded analogue such that there is a faithful embedding

$$ \mathbf{L}:\left\{\begin{tabular}[]{l}Quasi-coherent sheaves of\\
$\infty$-categories on $\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})^{\prime}$\\
\end{tabular}\right\}\hookrightarrow\left\{\begin{tabular}[]{l}$\infty$-categories with an\\
action of $\mathrm{Shv}(G(\!(t)\!);k)$\\
\end{tabular}\right\}^{\mathrm{gr}}\otimes_{\pi_{0}(k)}F $$

whose essential image consists of those $\mathrm{Shv}(G(\!(t)\!);k)$ -module categories which are generated by their $G[\![t]\!]$ -equivariant objects. This is similar in spirit to (a small part of) the local geometric Langlands correspondence. In particular, if $\mathcal{C}$ and $\mathcal{D}$ are quasi-coherent sheaves of $\infty$ -categories on $\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})^{\prime}$ , then there should be an equivalence

$$ \mathrm{Map}_{\mathrm{QCohCat}(\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})^{\prime})}(\mathcal{C},\mathcal{D})\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{Map}_{\mathrm{Shv}(G(\!(t)\!);k){\text{-}\mathrm{mod}}^{\mathrm{gr}}}(\mathbf{L}(\mathcal{C}),\mathbf{L}(\mathcal{D}))\otimes_{\pi_{0}(k)}F. $$

(One also expects a tamely-ramified variant of 1.6, where the left-hand side is replaced by the category of modules over $\QCoh(\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{P}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})^{\prime}\times_{\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})^{\prime}}\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{P}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})^{\prime})$ viewed as a monoidal category under convolution. The essential image of this functor would consist of those $\mathrm{Shv}(G(\!(t)\!);k)$ -module categories which are generated by their $I_{P}$ -equivariant objects.) Some examples of the value of $\mathbf{L}$ are given in Table 1. The calculations of [Dev3] also suggest additional lines in this table, at least when $k$ is connective complex K-theory.

The usual local geometric Langlands correspondence [FG] would relate the $(\infty,2)$ -category of $\infty$ -categories with an action of $\mathrm{Shv}(G(\!(t)\!))$ to the $(\infty,2)$ -category of ind-coherent sheaves of $\infty$ -categories on the moduli stack $\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{G}}}}(D^{\times})$ of ${\check{{G}}}$ -local systems on the punctured formal disk $D^{\times}$ . Let us try to informally explain the analogy between this and the generalized correspondence suggested above, where one must instead replace $\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{G}}}}(D^{\times})$ by $\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})^{\prime}$ . In the de Rham setting, $\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{G}}}}(D^{\times})$ can informally be viewed as the stack of maps from the (ill-defined) de Rham stack $D^{\times}_{\mathrm{dR}}$ of $D^{\times}$ to $B{\check{{G}}}$ . We are then suggesting that one should view $\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee}$ as analogous to $D^{\times}_{\mathrm{dR}}$ (or at least to a small part thereof).

In fact, this analogy is not new: if $\mathbf{G}_{0}$ was a $1$ -dimensional formal group (instead of an actual $1$ -dimensional algebraic group), then $\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee}$ has been studied in the homotopy theory literature [ST, MRT, Mou] as the “ $\mathbf{G}_{0}$ -circle” $S^{1}_{\mathbf{G}_{0}}$ , marketed as a $\mathbf{G}_{0}$ -analogue of the homotopy type of the usual circle. For instance, there should be an equivalence $R\Gamma(D^{\times}_{\mathrm{dR}};\mathcal{O})=R\Gamma_{\mathrm{dR}}(D^{\times})$ , so that its cohomology is an exterior algebra over $\mathbf{C}$ on a single class in cohomological degree $1$ . Similarly, the cohomology of $R\Gamma(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee};\mathcal{O})$ is also an exterior algebra over $\pi_{0}(k)$ on a single class in cohomological degree $1$ (but outside of characteristic zero, the derived algebra structures on $R\Gamma(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee};\mathcal{O})$ and $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{dR}}(D^{\times})$ generally disagree). Thus, the affinizations of $\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee}$ and $D^{\times}_{\mathrm{dR}}$ , at least, behave similarly. This suggests that $\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(\mathbf{G}_{0}^{\vee})^{\prime}$ behaves like a slight variant of (the formal neighborhood of the trivial local system in) $\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{G}}}}(D^{\times})$ .

Informally, 1.6 is suggesting that the $(\infty,2)$ -category of quasicoherent sheaves of $\infty$ -categories on $\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(S^{1}_{\mathbf{G}_{0}})$ should be a full subcategory of a graded analogue of the $(\infty,2)$ -category of $\infty$ -categories with $\mathrm{Shv}(G(\!(t)\!);k)$ -action. The latter is roughly the $(\infty,2)$ -category of $\infty$ -categories over the stack $\mathrm{Bun}_{G_{k}}(S^{1}_{k})$ of $G_{k}$ -bundles on the Betti stack (over $k$ ) of the topological circle44 4 Here, if $X$ is a suitably nice topological space, we write $X_{k}$ to denote the stack such that $\QCoh(X_{k})\simeq\mathrm{Shv}(X;k)$ .. Thus the Langlands duality of 1.6 “swaps” the topological circle $S^{1}$ (manifested as its Betti stack $S^{1}_{k}$ ) with the $\mathbf{G}_{0}$ -circle $S^{1}_{\mathbf{G}_{0}}$ . The merit of this perspective, especially in the context of topological quantum field theories [KW, BZSV], is completely unclear to me.

### 1.4. Outline and other results

We now give an overview of the content of this article. In Section 2, we briefly review the derived geometric Satake and the Arkhipov-Bezrukavnikov-Ginzburg equivalences, and show how to deduce the corresponding statements 1.1 and 1.2 over the regular loci.

Motivated by the issue of decompleting Borel-equivariant cohomology (which appears naturally in studying the derived geometric Satake and the Arkhipov-Bezrukavnikov-Ginzburg equivalences), we recall in Section 3 the setup of (genuine) equivariant generalized cohomology following [Lur1, GM1, GM2]. For a compact abelian group $T_{c}$ and a finite $T_{c}$ -space $X$ , we also introduce the category $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(X;k)$ of equivariant local systems of $k$ -modules on $X$ for an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring $k$ equipped with an “oriented” $1$ -dimensional commutative group scheme $\mathbf{G}$ . This section also reviews/generalizes the all-important Atiyah-Bott localization theorem [AB], and the corresponding results of Goresky-Kottwitz-MacPherson [GKM].

In Section 4, we introduce the degeneration $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ of the $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ that we discussed in the preceding subsection, and also discuss the definition of this $\infty$ -category for the non-complex-oriented ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring $\mathrm{KO}$ . The definition of $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ depends only on the equivariant homology $k^{T_{c}}_{\ast}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G})$ (denoted by $\pi_{\ast}\mathcal{F}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G})^{\vee}$ in the body of this article) as a coalgebra/Hopf algebroid over the equivariant cohomology $\pi_{\ast}k_{T_{c}}$ of a point.

The next Section 5 is essentially purely combinatorial: it studies the case when $G$ is a torus $T$ , and imposes the additional data of loop-rotation equivariance. In terms of the homotopy equivalence $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}\cong\Omega G_{c}$ , this comes from the $S^{1}$ -action on $\Omega G_{c}$ obtained by viewing it as $\Omega^{2}(BG_{c})=\mathrm{Map}_{\ast}(S^{2},BG_{c})$ and using the $S^{1}$ -action by rotation on $S^{2}$ . Namely, we show that if $k$ is an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring equipped with an “oriented” $1$ -dimensional commutative group scheme $\mathbf{G}$ , then $k^{T_{c}\times S^{1}_{\mathrm{rot}}}_{\ast}(\mathrm{Gr}_{T})$ (or really, its sheafification over $\Hom(\mathbb{X}^{\ast}(T),\mathbf{G})$ ) can be identified with a $\mathbf{G}$ -analogue of the Weyl algebra of the Langlands dual torus ${\check{{T}}}$ . For instance, if $k=\mathbf{Q}[u^{\pm 1}]$ and $\mathbf{G}=\mathbf{G}_{a}$ , then $k^{T_{c}\times S^{1}_{\mathrm{rot}}}_{\ast}(\mathrm{Gr}_{T})$ is the rescaled Weyl algebra of ${\check{{T}}}$ ; similarly, if $k=\mathrm{KU}$ and $\mathbf{G}=\mathbf{G}_{m}$ , then $k^{T_{c}\times S^{1}_{\mathrm{rot}}}_{\ast}(\mathrm{Gr}_{T})$ is the $q$ -Weyl algebra of the dual torus ${\check{{T}}}$ . We also explain the relationship between this $\mathbf{G}$ -analogue of the Weyl algebra of ${\check{{T}}}$ and the “ $F$ -de Rham complex” of [DM].

In Section 6, we review the classical story concerning $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ when $k=\mathbf{Q}[u^{\pm 1}]$ . The purpose of this section is to reprove the results of [BFM, YZ2] using only techniques amenable to generalization to other equivariant cohomology theories. In particular, in Corollary 6.8, we reprove the equivalence between $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ and $\QCoh(\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}^{\mathrm{reg}}/{\check{{G}}})$ . The remainder of Section 6 is concerned with the question of loop-rotation equivariance. Using results of [GKV2] and [Gin], we prove that $\mathrm{Loc}_{G_{c}\times S^{1}_{\mathrm{rot}}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ can be identified with a certain localization of the Harish-Chandra category $\mathrm{HC}^{\hbar}_{{\check{{G}}}}=U_{\hbar}({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}){\text{-}\mathrm{mod}}^{({\check{{G}}},\mathrm{weak})}$ . This line of argument is, in some sense, precisely the opposite of that of [Lon2].

We finally turn to the K-theoretic story in Section 7. Corollary 7.10 therein states that $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ is equivalent to $\QCoh(\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{reg}}/{\check{{G}}})$ when $G$ is connected, almost simple, and simply-laced; in this section, unlike in Theorem 1.4, the multiplicative Grothendieck-Springer resolution $\widetilde{{\check{{G}}}}$ is defined to be ${\check{{G}}}\times^{{\check{{B}}}}B$ (instead of ${\check{{G}}}\times^{{\check{{B}}}}{\check{{B}}}$ ). This is to be understood as analogous to the usual Grothendieck-Springer resolution $\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}$ , which is defined to be ${\check{{G}}}\times^{{\check{{B}}}}{\check{{\mathfrak{n}}}}^{\perp}$ (as opposed to ${\check{{G}}}\times^{{\check{{B}}}}{\check{{\mathfrak{b}}}}$ ). We also briefly study the question of loop-rotation equivariance in Theorem 7.31 using degenerate affine nil-Hecke algebras, and phrase some precise expectations about the relationship to the representation theory of quantum groups; but we do not yet know how to prove these statements. In Proposition 7.25, we also study the effect under Langlands duality of complex conjugation on equivariant K-theory.

The elliptic story is studied in Section 8, where we use the important results of [Dav] to show in Corollary 8.11 that $\mathrm{Loc}_{{\check{{T}}}_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ is equivalent to a localization of $\QCoh(\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{B}}}}^{0}(E))$ when $G$ is connected, almost simple, and simply-laced. We also briefly study the question of loop-rotation equivariance in Theorem 8.21, but do not even know how to describe the expected Langlands dual story. It should, however, be related to the representation theory of elliptic quantum groups [Fel].

The remainder of this article is concerned with comparisons to (by now) classical constructions in equivariant algebraic topology. Section 9 studies the effect of “power operations” on $k$ under the Langlands duality of Theorem 1.4. These are additional symmetries of the ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring $k$ which yield the theory of Steenrod operations in ordinary cohomology and Adams operations in K-theory. (This is closely related to, but distinct from, work [Lon4] of Lonergan.) We review how the theory of isogenies of $\mathbf{G}_{0}$ controls power operations for $k$ , which is used to show that power operations for $k$ identify with natural “Artin-Schreier” type maps on ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}/{\check{{G}}}$ , ${\check{{G}}}/{\check{{G}}}$ , and $\mathrm{Bun}_{{\check{{G}}}}^{\mathrm{ss}}(E)$ . As an amusing application, we reprove that the restricted Lie operation vanishes on the nilpotent cone in characteristics at least the Coxeter number (see Proposition 9.15).

In Section 10, we explain how the degeneration of $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ to $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}^{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ should be viewed as analogous to the Hochschild-Kostant-Rosenberg degeneration of Hochschild homology to differential forms. (See [Rak] for a modern take on this degeneration.) Using this perspective, we show how (when $G$ has torsion-free fundamental group) Theorem 1.4 recovers results of [BZ] identifying the conjugation-equivariant cohomologies $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G_{c}}(G_{c};\mathbf{Q})$ (resp. $\mathrm{KU}^{\ast}_{G_{c}}(G_{c})$ ) with the algebra of Kähler differentials on $\mathfrak{t}/\!\!/W$ (resp. $T/\!\!/W$ ); the same argument also describes the equivariant elliptic cohomology of $G_{c}$ in terms of the algebra of Kähler differentials on the moduli space of semistable degree zero $G$ -bundles on the elliptic curve.

In Appendix A, we show by explicit calculation that the group scheme $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ (as well as other classical geometric objects, like Grassmannians which are not projective spaces) cannot admit a natural lifting from $\mathbf{Z}$ to the sphere spectrum or even to connective complex K-theory. The argument goes by showing that $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ cannot admit a reasonable $\delta$ -structure (even mod $p$ ). This supplements a comment made in the beginning of Section 4.

The results of this article were motivated by the work of Hopkins-Kuhn-Ravenel [HKR] describing the generalized equivariant cohomology of finite groups. In Appendix B, we briefly review their results (and the corresponding categorifications, due to Lurie [Lur8]). Despite the case of finite groups being the diametric opposite to the case of connected compact Lie groups studied in this article, we give a heuristic argument showing that Theorem 1.4 can be viewed as an analogue of (some of) the results of [HKR, Lur8].

Another motivation for the results of this article came from physics. Namely, the equivariant homology of $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ describes the Coulomb branch of $3$ d $\mathcal{N}=4$ pure gauge theory [BFN], and one expects that the generalized equivariant $\mathrm{KU}$ -homology (resp. elliptic homology) of $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ is related to the Coulomb branch of $4$ d $\mathcal{N}=2$ (resp. $5$ d $\mathcal{N}=1$ ) pure gauge theory. We briefly review this story in Appendix C, and give explicit generators and relations for the Coulomb branches of $3$ d $\mathcal{N}=4$ and $4$ d $\mathcal{N}=2$ pure gauge theories with gauge groups $\mathrm{SL}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{PGL}_{2}$ . The $4$ -dimensional case is a $q$ -analogue of the quantization of the Atiyah-Hitchin manifold [AH] from [BDG, Equation 5.51].

### 1.5. Notation and terminology

In most of this article, $G$ will denote a connected, almost simple, and simply-laced algebraic group over $\mathbf{C}$ , and $B$ will denote a Borel subgroup therein. If $H$ is a reductive algebraic group over $\mathbf{C}$ , we will write $H_{c}$ to denote the maximal compact subgroup of the complex Lie group $H(\mathbf{C})$ , so $H_{c}$ is a compact Lie group. We will use the terminology “finite $H_{c}$ -space” to mean a finite $H_{c}$ -CW complex. I have tried to be careful to add the subscript $c$ where necessary, but some omissions have certainly inevitably crept in.

The symbol $k$ will denote an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring which will generally be fixed at the beginning of each section/theorem statement. The symbol $F$ will denote an algebraically closed field with a map $\pi_{0}(k)\to F$ . If $H$ is a group scheme acting on a scheme $Y$ , the symbol $Y/H$ will mean the stacky quotient, and $Y/\!\!/H$ will denote the invariant-theoretic quotient. The Langlands dual group ${\check{{G}}}$ will generally be defined over $F$ ; if we wish to view it as defined over a commutative ring $R$ , we will denote it by ${\check{{G}}}_{R}$ . If $T$ is a torus, we will write $\mathbb{X}^{\ast}(T)$ and $\mathbb{X}_{\ast}(T)$ to denote its lattice of characters and cocharacters. We will also write ${\check{{\Lambda}}}$ to denote the root lattice of $G$ and $\Lambda$ to denote the coroot lattice of $G$ . The symbol $\widetilde{T}$ will denote the extended torus $T\times\mathbf{G}_{m}^{\mathrm{rot}}$ . If ${\check{{N}}}\subseteq{\check{{G}}}$ is the unipotent radical of a Borel subgroup of ${\check{{G}}}$ , we will write $\psi:{\check{{\mathfrak{n}}}}\to\mathbf{G}_{a}$ to denote a nondegenerate character of ${\check{{\mathfrak{n}}}}$ , i.e., an additive character which is nonzero on each simple root space. If $X$ is an ${\check{{N}}}$ -scheme, we will write $T^{\ast}(X/_{\psi}{\check{{N}}})$ to denote the Hamiltonian reduction of $T^{\ast}X$ at $\psi$ (that is, if $\mu:T^{\ast}(X)\to{\check{{\mathfrak{n}}}}^{\ast}$ is the moment map, then $T^{\ast}(X/_{\psi}{\check{{N}}})\cong\mu^{-1}(\psi)/{\check{{N}}}$ ).

Finally, we will write $\mathcal{S}$ to denote the $\infty$ -category of spaces (also known as “anima”, but we will not use this terminology here). The symbols $\QCoh$ , $\mathrm{Mod}$ , etc. are all to be understood in the derived sense, as are all fiber and tensor products; we will make it clear if any of these operations are to be understood in their classical sense. In particular, if $X$ is a scheme or stack, we will write $\QCoh(X)^{\heartsuit}$ to denote the abelian category of quasicoherent sheaves on $X$ . If $A$ is an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring, $\mathcal{C}$ is an $A$ -linear $\infty$ -category (that is, a $\mathrm{Mod}_{A}$ -module in the $\infty$ -category of presentable stable $\infty$ -categories), and $A\to B$ is a map of ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -rings, then $\mathcal{C}\otimes_{A}B$ will denote the $B$ -linear $\infty$ -category $\mathcal{C}\otimes_{\mathrm{Mod}_{A}}\mathrm{Mod}_{B}$ ; similarly if $A$ is a classical commutative ring and $\mathcal{C}$ is an abelian $A$ -linear category.

## 2. The regular locus

In this section, we will quickly review the derived geometric Satake equivalence following [BF] and [AG]. Let $k$ denote a commutative $\mathbf{Q}$ -algebra; all Langlands dual objects will be assumed to live over $k$ , and are base-changes of their “split forms” over $\mathbf{Q}$ .

#### Setup 2.1.

Let $G$ be a connected reductive group (over $\mathbf{C}$ , always), and let $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}=G(\!(t)\!)/G[\![t]\!]$ denote the affine Grassmannian. There is a canonical left action of $G(\!(t)\!)$ on $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ , and hence an action of $G[\![t]\!]\subseteq G(\!(t)\!)$ . The affine Grassmannian is a union of $G[\![t]\!]$ -invariant closed subschemes $X_{\alpha}$ of finite type, and one defines $\mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)=\colim_{\alpha}\mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}(X_{\alpha};k)$ . Inside $\mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ are two full subcategories:

- • $\mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)^{\mathrm{lcc}}$ is the full subcategory of objects whose image under the forgetful functor $\mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)\to\mathrm{Shv}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ is compact. Such objects are called “locally compact”.

- • $\mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)^{\omega}$ of compact objects in $\mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ .

The $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ admits a monoidal structure, which in fact restricts to a monoidal structure on each of the full subcategories above.

#### Setup 2.2.

Let $(e,f,h)$ denote a principal $\mathfrak{sl}_{2}$ -triple in the Langlands dual Lie algebra ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}$ . The element $f$ defines a nondegenerate character $\psi:{\check{{\mathfrak{n}}}}\to\mathbf{A}^{1}$ . Let ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast,e}$ denote the orthogonal complement to the subspace $[e,{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}]\subseteq{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}$ . This defines the Kostant slice $\psi+{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast,e}\subseteq{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}$ ; we will denote this inclusion by $\kappa$ . Composing the invariant-theoretic quotient map $\chi:{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}\to{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}$ with the Kostant slice defines an isomorphism. In other words, the following composite is an isomorphism:

$$ \psi+{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast,e}\xrightarrow{{\kappa}}{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}\xrightarrow{{\chi}}{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}. $$

It will be convenient to identify $\psi+{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast,e}$ with ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}$ under this isomorphism. If the vector space ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}$ is placed in weight $2$ , the map $\kappa$ can be checked to give a graded map

$$ \kappa:{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}\to{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}(2). $$

Shearing this graded map (in the sense of [Dev3, Section 2.1]) defines a map ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}[2]/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}\to{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}[2]$ , which we will also denote by $\kappa$ .

#### Lemma 2.3 (Chevalley restriction).

There is an isomorphism ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}\cong\mathfrak{t}/\!\!/W$ , which refines to an isomorphism of graded schemes

$$ {\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}(2)/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}\cong\mathfrak{t}(2)/\!\!/W\cong\spec\mathrm{H}^{\ast}_{G}(\ast;\mathbf{C}). $$

The first part of the following result is [BF, Theorem 5], and the second part is [AG, Theorem 12.5.3].

#### Theorem 2.4 (Bezrukavnikov-Finkelberg, Arinkin-Gaitsgory).

There is a monoidal equivalence

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)^{\mathrm{lcc}}\simeq\mathrm{Perf}({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}[2]/{\check{{G}}}), $$

which restricts to a monoidal equivalence

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)^{\omega}\simeq\mathrm{Perf}_{{\check{{\mathcal{N}}}}/{\check{{G}}}}({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}[2]/{\check{{G}}}), $$

where the right-hand side is the full subcategory of those perfect complexes which are set-theoretically supported on the nilpotent cone of ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}$ . Furthermore, there is a commutative diagram

$$ \textstyle{\mathrm{Ind}(\mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)^{\mathrm{lcc}})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{\sim} \scriptstyle{p_{!}} \textstyle{\QCoh({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}[2]/{\check{{G}}})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{\kappa^{\ast}} \textstyle{\mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\ast;k)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{\sim} \textstyle{\QCoh({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}[2]/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}),} $$

where $p:\mathrm{Gr}_{G}\to\ast$ is the canonical map to a point and $\kappa^{\ast}$ is pullback along the (shifted) Kostant slice.

We will refer to the first equivalence of Theorem 2.4 as the derived geometric Satake equivalence, or more colloquially as “derived Satake”.

#### Definition 2.5.

A point $x\in{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}$ is called regular if its centralizer $Z_{{\check{{G}}}}(x)\subseteq{\check{{G}}}$ has dimension given by the rank of ${\check{{G}}}$ . Let ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast,\mathrm{reg}}$ denote the locus of regular elements; this is an open subscheme whose complement is of codimension $3$ .

#### Theorem 2.6 (Kostant, [Kos1]).

The ${\check{{G}}}$ -orbit of the Kostant slice $\kappa:{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}\to{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}$ identifies with the regular locus ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast,\mathrm{reg}}$ .

#### Corollary 2.7.

Let $\underline{k}_{\mathrm{Gr}_{G}}\in\mathrm{Ind}(\mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)^{\mathrm{lcc}})$ denote the constant sheaf, and let $\mathrm{Loc}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ denote the full subcategory generated by $\underline{k}_{\mathrm{Gr}_{G}}$ . Then there is an equivalence

$$ \mathrm{Loc}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)\simeq\QCoh({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast,\mathrm{reg}}[2]/{\check{{G}}}). $$

#### Proof.

Observe that $\underline{k}_{\mathrm{Gr}_{G}}$ is the pullback $p^{\ast}\underline{k}$ of the (necessarily constant) sheaf $\underline{k}\in\mathrm{Shv}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\ast;k)$ . Since $p^{\ast}$ is the right adjoint to $p_{!}$ (and $\kappa_{\ast}$ is the right adjoint to $\kappa^{\ast}$ ), the commutative diagram of Theorem 2.4 says that $\mathrm{Loc}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ is equivalent to the full subcategory of $\QCoh({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}[2]/{\check{{G}}})$ generated by $\kappa_{\ast}\mathcal{O}_{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}[2]/\!\!/{\check{{G}}}}$ . However, Theorem 2.6 implies that this full subcategory is equivalent to $\QCoh({\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast,\mathrm{reg}}[2]/{\check{{G}}})$ , as desired. ∎

A parallel story holds for the Arkhipov-Bezrukavnikov-Ginzburg (called “ABG” in this article) equivalence from [ABG].

#### Recollection 2.8.

Let $\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}$ denote the Grothendieck-Springer resolution, so that $\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}=T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})/{\check{{T}}}$ . The action of ${\check{{G}}}$ on $T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})$ defines the moment map $\mu:\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}\to{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}$ . Let $\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}^{\mathrm{reg}}$ denote the preimage of the regular locus ${\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast,\mathrm{reg}}\subseteq{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}$ under the moment map $\mu$ .

#### Proposition 2.9.

There is an isomorphism $\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}\cong{\check{{G}}}\times^{{\check{{B}}}}{\check{{\mathfrak{n}}}}^{\perp}$ , as well as a map $\kappa:\psi+{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}\subseteq{\check{{\mathfrak{n}}}}^{\perp}$ which fits into a Cartesian square

$$ \textstyle{\psi+{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{{\check{{\mathfrak{n}}}}^{\perp}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{\mu} \textstyle{\psi+{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast,e}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}.} $$

#### Proof.

Let ${\check{{M}}}$ be a Hamiltonian ${\check{{G}}}$ -scheme with moment map $\mu:{\check{{M}}}\to{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}$ . Then the pullback ${\check{{M}}}\times_{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}}(\psi+{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast,e})$ can be identified with the Whittaker reduction ${\check{{M}}}/_{\psi}{\check{{N}}}$ . Indeed, a theorem of Kostant’s from [Kos2] identifies $\psi+{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast,e}$ with $(\psi+{\check{{\mathfrak{n}}}}^{-,\perp})/{\check{{N}}}^{-}$ , so that there are isomorphisms

$$ \displaystyle{\check{{M}}}\times_{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}}(\psi+{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast,e}) \displaystyle\cong{\check{{M}}}/{\check{{G}}}\times_{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/{\check{{G}}}}(\psi+{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast,e}) \displaystyle\cong{\check{{M}}}/{\check{{G}}}\times_{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}^{\ast}/{\check{{G}}}}(\psi+{\check{{\mathfrak{n}}}}^{-,\perp})/{\check{{N}}}^{-} \displaystyle\cong({\check{{M}}}\times_{{\check{{\mathfrak{n}}}}^{-,\ast}}\{\psi\})/{\check{{N}}}^{-}={\check{{M}}}/_{\psi}{\check{{N}}}^{-}. $$

Therefore, the fiber product in the statement of the proposition identifies with the Whittaker reduction $\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}/_{\psi}{\check{{N}}}^{-}$ . Since $\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}\cong T^{\ast}({\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})/{\check{{T}}}$ , we may identify $\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}/_{\psi}{\check{{N}}}^{-}$ with the quotient by ${\check{{T}}}$ of $T^{\ast}({\check{{N}}}^{-}{}_{\psi}\backslash{\check{{G}}}/{\check{{N}}})$ . Since Whittaker functions are supported on the big cell, this twisted cotangent bundle is in turn isomorphic to $T^{\ast}({\check{{N}}}^{-}{}_{\psi}\backslash({\check{{N}}}^{-}\times{\check{{T}}}\times{\check{{N}}})/{\check{{N}}})\cong{\check{{T}}}\times(\psi+{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast})$ . The desired Cartesian square follows. ∎

Again, $\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}$ admits a $\mathbf{G}_{m}$ -action obtained by placing ${\check{{\mathfrak{n}}}}^{\perp}$ in weight $2$ , and the map $\kappa:{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}\to{\check{{\mathfrak{n}}}}^{\perp}$ is equivariant if ${\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}$ is also placed in weight $2$ . Therefore, shearing (as in [Dev3, Section 2.1]) defines a map

$$ {\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}[2]\xrightarrow{{\kappa}}{\check{{\mathfrak{n}}}}^{\perp}[2]\to\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}[2]. $$

We will sometimes denote this composite also by $\kappa$ .

The first part of the below equivalence was proved by Arkhipov-Bezrukavnikov-Ginzburg in [ABG]; the commutative diagram below follows from Proposition 2.9 and Theorem 2.4.

#### Theorem 2.10.

Let $B\subseteq G$ be a Borel subgroup, and let $I=G[\![t]\!]\times_{G}B$ denote the associated Iwahori subgroup. Then there is an equivalence

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{I}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)^{\mathrm{lcc}}\simeq\mathrm{Perf}(\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}[2]/{\check{{G}}}), $$

which restricts to a monoidal equivalence

$$ \mathrm{Shv}_{I}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)^{\omega}\simeq\mathrm{Perf}_{{{\check{{\mathcal{N}}}}}/{\check{{G}}}}(\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}[2]/{\check{{G}}}). $$

Furthermore, there is a commutative diagram

$$ \textstyle{\mathrm{Ind}(\mathrm{Shv}_{I}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)^{\mathrm{lcc}})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{\sim} \scriptstyle{p_{!}} \textstyle{\QCoh(\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}[2]/{\check{{G}}})\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{\kappa^{\ast}} \textstyle{\mathrm{Shv}_{I}(\ast;k)\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{\sim} \textstyle{\QCoh({\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}[2]),} $$

where $p:\mathrm{Gr}_{G}\to\ast$ is the canonical map to a point and $\kappa^{\ast}$ is pullback along the (shifted) Kostant slice.

As in Corollary 2.7, we find:

#### Corollary 2.11.

Let $\underline{k}_{\mathrm{Gr}_{G}}\in\mathrm{Shv}_{I}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ denote the constant sheaf, and let $\mathrm{Loc}_{I}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ denote the full subcategory generated by $\underline{k}_{\mathrm{Gr}_{G}}$ . Then there is an equivalence

$$ \mathrm{Loc}_{I}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)\simeq\QCoh(\widetilde{{\check{{\mathfrak{g}}}}}^{\mathrm{reg}}[2]/{\check{{G}}}). $$

The constant sheaf has singular support given by the zero section. In fact, the $\infty$ -categories $\mathrm{Loc}_{G[\![t]\!]}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ and $\mathrm{Loc}_{I}(\mathrm{Gr}_{G};k)$ are the subcategories of locally constant (equivariant) sheaves on $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ . As such, they depend only on the underlying homotopy types of $G[\![t]\!]$ , $I$ , and $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ .

#### Notation 2.12.

Let $G_{c}$ be the maximal compact subgroup of $G(\mathbf{C})$ , and let $T_{c}$ be the maximal torus of $G_{c}$ corresponding to the Borel $B$ . It is not difficult to see that there are homotopy equivalences

$$ \displaystyle G[\![t]\!] \displaystyle\simeq G(\mathbf{C})\simeq G_{c} \displaystyle I \displaystyle\simeq B(\mathbf{C})\simeq T_{c}. $$

The homotopy type of $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ follows from the next result, due to Quillen and Garland-Raghunathan:

#### Theorem 2.13 (Quillen, Garland-Raghunathan, [GR2, Mit]).

There is a homotopy equivalence $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}\simeq\Omega G_{c}$ (and a homeomorphism onto the subspace of $\Omega G_{c}$ on those based loops with polynomial Fourier expansion) which is equivariant for the left-action of $G_{c}\subseteq G(\mathbf{C})\subseteq G(\mathbf{C}[\![t]\!])$ on the left-hand side and the action of $G_{c}$ on the right-hand side by conjugation.

In our discussion below, we will mostly be concerned with the homology of $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ , in which case we may replace $\mathrm{Gr}_{G}$ by $\Omega G_{c}$ . To this extent, we will implicitly use Theorem 2.13 without further mention. We will describe analogues of the equivalences of Corollary 2.7 and Corollary 2.11 for equivariant K-theory and equivariant elliptic cohomology.

## 3. Equivariant cohomology and the case of tori

In order to study and prove analogues of the equivalences of Corollary 2.7 and Corollary 2.11 for other cohomology theories, we need to review some foundational aspects of the theory of equivariant cohomology. I have reviewed some of the basics of equivariant K-theory in [Dev3, Section 2.2]. The theory of equivariant elliptic cohomology is developed similarly, and we will now describe this story (in a somewhat leisurely fashion) following [Lur1, GM2, GM1]. At the end of this section, we describe the geometric Satake equivalence for tori.

The basic question we will address is giving a definition of the $\infty$ -category $\mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(X;k)$ for a $T_{c}$ -space $X$ for a sufficiently general ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -ring $k$ . When $k$ is an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathbf{Q}$ -algebra, Theorem 2.10 requires that there is an equivalence

$$ \mathrm{Loc}_{T_{c}}(\ast;k)\simeq\QCoh({\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}[2]). $$

One often defines the $\infty$ -category of $k$ -modules on a space $X$ as the $\infty$ -category $\Fun(X,\mathrm{Mod}_{k})$ . However, when $X=BT_{c}$ , the $\infty$ -category $\Fun(BT_{c},\mathrm{Mod}_{k})$ does not agree with $\QCoh({\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}[2])$ ; instead, it only agrees with a certain completion of this $\infty$ -category, as we will now explain.

#### Lemma 3.1.

Let $k$ be an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ -algebra. Then there is an equivalence

$$ \Fun(BT_{c},\mathrm{Mod}_{k})\simeq\mathrm{IndCoh}(\{1\}\times_{{\check{{T}}}}\{1\}). $$

If, moreover, $k$ is an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathbf{Q}$ -algebra, this can be rewritten as an equivalence

$$ \Fun(BT_{c},\mathrm{Mod}_{k})\simeq\QCoh(\widehat{{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}}^{\ast}[2]), $$

where $\widehat{{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}}^{\ast}$ denotes the completion of ${\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}^{\ast}$ at the origin.

#### Proof.

If $X$ is a finite space, there is an equivalence $\Fun(X,\mathrm{Mod}_{k})\simeq\mathrm{IndCoh}_{C_{\ast}(\Omega X;k)}$ , where $C_{\ast}(\Omega X;k)$ is the ${\mathbf{E}_{{1}}}$ - $k$ -algebra of $k$ -chains on the based loop space $\Omega X$ . When $X=BT_{c}$ , we may identify $\Omega X=T_{c}$ . Recall that $T_{c}$ is the classifying space of the lattice $\mathbb{X}_{\ast}(T)$ , so that there is an equivalence

$$ C_{\ast}(T_{c};k)\cong k\otimes_{C_{\ast}(\mathbb{X}_{\ast}(T);k)}k. $$

Of course, we may identify $C_{\ast}(\mathbb{X}_{\ast}(T);k)\cong k[\mathbb{X}_{\ast}(T)]$ with the ring of functions on ${\check{{T}}}$ . Therefore, $\spec C_{\ast}(T_{c};k)\cong\{1\}\times_{{\check{{T}}}}\{1\}$ , as desired.

Koszul duality gives an equivalence $\mathrm{IndCoh}(C_{\ast}(T_{c};k))\to\QCoh(C^{\ast}(BT_{c};k))$ given by $M\mapsto\Hom_{C_{\ast}(T_{c};k)}(k,M)$ . If $k$ is an ${\mathbf{E}_{\infty}}$ - $\mathbf{Q}$ -algebra, then $C^{\ast}(BT_{c};k)$ is formal, and so it can be identified with the shearing of $\mathrm{H}^{\ast}(BT_{c};k)$ . But

$$ \spf\mathrm{H}^{\ast}(BT_{c};k)\cong\widehat{\mathfrak{t}}(2)\cong\widehat{{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}}^{\ast}(2), $$

so $\mathrm{IndCoh}(C_{\ast}(T_{c};k))$ is equivalent to $\QCoh(\widehat{{\check{{\mathfrak{t}}}}}^{\ast}[2])$ , as desired. ∎

#### Example 3.2.

Suppose $T_{c}=S^{1}$ . Then Lemma 3.1 tells us that $\Fun(BS^{1},\mathrm{Mod}_{k})\simeq\QCoh(\widehat{\mathbf{A}^{1}}[2])$ ; the equivalence sends a functor $BS^{1}\to\mathrm{Mod}_{k}$ , regarded as a $k$ -module $M$ with $S^{1}$ -action, to its homotopy invariants $M^{hS^{1}}$ . Let $t\in\pi_{-2}(k^{hS^{1}})$ denote a generator. Observe that if $a_{\lambda}:k\to k[2]$ denotes the boundary map in the cofiber sequence $k[1]\to C_{\ast}(S^{1};k)\to k$ , the homotopy invariants of $k[a_{\lambda}^{-1}]$ are simply $k^{hS^{1}}[t^{-1}]$ (i.e., the Tate construction). In particular, $\pi_{\ast}(k[a_{\lambda}^{-1}])^{hS^{1}}\cong\pi_{\ast}(k)(\!(t)\!)$ .
